basic_info.title: Ontology-based Processing of Dynamic Maps in Automated Driving
basic_info.venue: Proceedings of the 12th International Joint Conference on Knowledge Discovery, Knowledge Engineering and Knowledge Management (IC3K 2020) - Volume 2: KEOD, pp. 98-107, SCITEPRESS. DOI: 10.5220/0010133900980107. Affiliations: BMW Car IT GmbH / Institute of Artificial Intelligence, University of Ulm.

method.input_representation: HD_map / map_data_formats / road_environment_model (low-level format ontologies abstracted to a high-level road-environment ontology; processed as map data streams)
method.graph_integration: KG_RDF_semantics (OWL 2 RL ontologies, RDF triples, Datalog rules, SPARQL queries)
method.notes: Knowledge-spatial architecture for a MOVING vehicle: continuous spatial reasoning using a spatial-window concept (forward/backward parameters) with spatial expiration (stream-like) over the road-environment ontology. Rules classified as primitive, transfer, spatial, and algorithmic. Evaluated for scalability in the SmartMapApp prototype using the RDFox reasoner.

gap_analysis.whats_missing: Implements the P1b semantic-enrichment idea SYMBOLICALLY via OWL 2 RL ontologies, Datalog rules and SPARQL spatial reasoning rather than as learned vectorized tokens in a transformer. Although it reasons over a moving vehicle along a route via spatial windows, it does so by logical inference, not as a learned map-matching or path-prediction task, and involves no sequence learning and no label-free training.
gap_analysis.novelty_vs_recombination: real_gap: orthogonal symbolic stream-reasoning paradigm and a BMW in-house precedent, distinct from and not a precursor to the proposed learned transformer+latent-RL hybrid.

relevance.bmw_relevance: HIGH - BMW's in-house ontology-based dynamic-map processing, authored by the thesis interview lead Adel Ayara with Birte Glimm, defining BMW's symbolic spatial road-environment reasoning for a moving vehicle.
